Question: What is the theme in the Star Wars movie?
Old_Answer: For each of the first 6: 1 The Phantom Menace So, as for a theme, I would say there was not much of the theme. George didn’t want another OT, he wanted to make new types of movies. Hence the prequels were additions, not standalone. But aside from the most important part of the film that is - in my opinion - Anakin’s father figure/the road he will go down, I would say the movie has a focus on destiny. Can it be stopped? Does anything need to happen for it to come true? 2 Attack of the Clones This was where all the pieces fell into place for checkmate. Whereas TPM was the set up. If I had to pick a theme, I would go with “small seeds, massive trees”. Tiny little manipulations and events violently shaking the galaxy’s fate. Small things in Anakin’s life shape him while large moves are made also. (This was way more focused on the Star Wars universe than sending messages to ours) 3 Revenge of the Sith Dread it, run from it… The theme was about a hero’s fall. No one is truly immune to temptation and that, sadly, emotions can lead you to a dark path if you let them control you. 4 A New Hope This was classical storytelling! It followed one of the best executions of the hero's journey. The theme also revolved a little bit around destiny, but mostly never judge a book by its cover. Any farm boy could become a galaxy’s hero. 5 The Empire Strikes Back Facing your fear. That’s my takeaway (in hindsight) Even though Luke lost the fight with Vader, I’d say Luke walked away with a victory as well. “A coward dies a thousand times before his death, but the valiant taste of death but once. It seems to me most strange that men should fear, seeing that death, a necessary end, will come when it will come.” - Shakespear’s Julius Caesar 6 Return of the Jedi This one had the strongest theme in my eyes: redemption. It doesn’t matter what your past was if you’re willing to put it behind you, where it belongs. Someone will always see the good in you and it will always be there. And it will always be ready to take over.
